derivation_notes: For the reversible reaction R + L <-> RL, rapid mass-action equilibrium gives K_d = [R][L]/[RL]. Combining this with the fixed receptor-pool balance [R]_total = [R] + [RL] yields f_bound = [RL]/[R]_total = L/(K_d + L).

domain_mechanisms.description: finite receptor occupancy or saturating signal transduction

scenario_text: Cultured cells are exposed to independently chosen concentrations of an extracellular ligand, and the immediate fraction of surface receptors in the ligand-bound signaling state is measured. Receptor abundance and cellular background are held fixed across samples. Binding is treated as rapidly equilibrated relative to receptor internalization and downstream signaling. The response should increase with ligand concentration and approach a finite occupancy ceiling.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.n_H: 1 <= n_H <= 4 for positive cooperativity; n_H = 1 recovers the parent independent-binding law

derivation_notes: The independent one-site Langmuir assumption is relaxed to an effective cooperative rapid-equilibrium binding/activation law, yielding a Hill-form occupancy with unchanged finite saturation ceiling. This remains a static mapping because binding is still assumed fast relative to downstream processes and receptor abundance/background remain fixed.
change_summary: The response law changes from a fixed-shape hyperbola to a Hill-like saturating curve by introducing an effective cooperativity exponent n_H. This specifically alters dose-response curvature: lower low-dose occupancy and a sharper transition near K_d when n_H > 1.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: All receptors have equivalent and independent ligand-binding sites.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Effective cooperativity in ligand binding or receptor activation, such as receptor clustering or multistep activation, producing a Hill-type occupancy curve under rapid equilibrium.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Setting n_H = 1 recovers the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: With fixed K_d, f_bound = L/(K_d + L) is a one-site Langmuir isotherm with a single shared half-saturation scale and fixed concave-down rise in L.
response_change.child_relation: Relax the assumption of equivalent independent binding by allowing cooperative binding, so the occupancy curve becomes Hill-like in L with a tunable low-L suppression and sharper mid-range transition while remaining saturating.
response_change.observable_effect: Across varying ligand concentration L with receptor abundance and background fixed, the child shows weaker response at low L and a steeper rise near intermediate L than the parent, which cannot match both regions simultaneously with one shared K_d.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Most visible when L spans well below to well above K_d, especially around the transition regime L ~ K_d; negligible distinction if measurements only cover an asymptotically low- or high-ligand regime.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate-dose points can reveal a sharper-than-hyperbolic bend; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger low-dose suppression and a more switch-like approach to saturation over a broader L range.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: In the noncooperative limit, the refined model reduces to the parent law.
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Effective cooperativity in ligand binding or receptor activation, producing a Hill-type occupancy curve under rapid equilibrium.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This is structurally harder than coefficient-only correction because n_H changes the shape class of the input-output map, not just its horizontal scale: it modifies low-dose asymptotics and mid-range slope while preserving bounded saturation.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: All receptors have equivalent and independent ligand-binding sites.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: Binding/activation is allowed to be effectively cooperative, so occupancy follows a Hill-type rapid-equilibrium law.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: When L is varied across the transition scale with receptor abundance and background held fixed, the parent predicts a single hyperbolic rise with fixed curvature, whereas the child predicts lower occupancy for L << K_d and a steeper transition near L ~ K_d for n_H > 1, while still saturating toward one as L >> K_d. This changes the scored target mapping itself, not only any unobserved auxiliary quantity.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set only shifts the hyperbola through K_d and cannot simultaneously reproduce both stronger low-dose suppression and sharper mid-range rise over the same admissible L range. Thus coefficient retuning of the parent cannot absorb the cooperative curvature change when measurements span below and around K_d.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Most visible when L spans well below to well above K_d, especially around the transition regime L ~ K_d; negligible distinction if measurements only cover an asymptotically low- or high-ligand regime.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate-dose points can reveal a sharper-than-hyperbolic bend; in holdout, the same mechanism extends to stronger low-dose suppression and a more switch-like approach to saturation over a broader L range.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: In the noncooperative limit, the refined model reduces to the parent law.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes all receptor binding events are equivalent and independent, omitting plausible effective cooperativity or receptor-clustering effects that alter the dose-response curvature without violating bounded monotone saturation.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: All receptors have equivalent and independent ligand-binding sites.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Effective cooperativity in ligand binding or receptor activation, producing a Hill-type occupancy curve under rapid equilibrium.
evolution_plan.rationale: The parent target mapping is a fixed-shape hyperbola: varying L while holding receptor abundance, background, and environment fixed changes occupancy through one shared threshold K_d and a predetermined curvature. A realistic next refinement is to relax independent-site binding and allow effective cooperativity, which changes the scored mapping itself rather than only auxiliary quantities. Under admissible conditions where L is sampled across the transition scale around K_d, the child predicts a more sigmoidal monotone rise: lower occupancy than the parent at subthreshold L, a steeper mid-range increase, and the same bounded saturation near one at high L. A single refitted parent K_d can shift the curve left or right but cannot simultaneously reproduce both the enhanced low-dose suppression and the sharper mid-range slope across those conditions. This contrast is scientifically meaningful when receptor clustering or multistep activation makes binding effectively non-independent; if data only cover a narrow regime far from K_d, the difference may be weakly identifiable.

new_symbol_range_suggestions.C: 0 <= C <= 1e4; activate competition when C is comparable to K_i

derivation_notes: A second extracellular species is introduced as a competitive binder sharing the same receptor pool, implemented by multiplicatively modulating the existing dissociation scale. When competitor is absent or very weakly binding, the modulation collapses and the parent Hill law is recovered.
change_summary: The original single-input Hill occupancy law is extended by a competitor-conditioned threshold shift. This creates a joint dependence on ligand and competitor concentrations while preserving monotone increase in L and a finite occupancy ceiling.

add_term_audit.mechanism_claim: An extracellular competitor or antagonist binds the same receptor pool and reduces occupancy by the measured ligand at rapid equilibrium.
add_term_audit.parent_reduction: Set C = 0, or take K_i to infinity so that C/K_i is negligible, and the modulation disappears to recover the parent Hill law.
add_term_audit.observable_signature: At fixed L, increasing competitor decreases f_bound; across competitor levels, the L-response curves are right-shifted with different apparent half-maximal positions while retaining a finite saturation ceiling.

response_change.parent_relation: With only L varying and K_d,n_H fixed across samples, f_bound is a single Hill curve of ligand concentration with one shared threshold and slope.
response_change.child_relation: Introduce competition by a second independently varied extracellular species so the apparent occupancy by the measured ligand becomes a joint function of ligand and competitor concentrations, shifting the ligand-response rightward as competitor increases while preserving bounded monotone saturation in L.
response_change.observable_effect: At fixed L, increasing competitor lowers f_bound; equivalently, the L dose-response curves for different competitor levels have different effective half-maximal positions that a single parent Hill curve cannot match simultaneously.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when an extracellular competing binder is present at concentrations comparable to its affinity so that competition measurably perturbs occupancy; negligible when competitor is absent or far below its dissociation scale.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, variation over L reveals the parent sigmoidal rise; in extended conditions with nonzero competitor, the same rise persists but is systematically shifted/suppressed across competitor levels, creating a conditional mapping not representable by one shared parent parameter set.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Setting competitor concentration to zero, or taking its affinity to be negligible, recovers the parent Hill law.
evolution_contract.promotion_reason: A competitive extracellular condition must vary between samples to generate an observable family of occupancy curves; with only L supplied and all parameters fixed, competition cannot be distinguished from a single refit of K_d on one condition.
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: competitive extracellular binding that modulates the effective ligand dissociation scale
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Competitive binding by a second extracellular ligand or antagonist that shares the receptor binding pool and reduces occupancy by the measured ligand under rapid equilibrium.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: The added competitor input multiplicatively modulates the existing threshold process, producing a family of conditional dose-response curves rather than one global Hill mapping. This cannot be reproduced by a coefficient-only correction when one shared parameter set must apply across all competitor conditions.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The extracellular binding environment is fixed and only the measured ligand determines rapid-equilibrium occupancy.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: A second independently sampled extracellular competitor modulates the effective binding threshold through shared receptor competition while rapid equilibrium and finite occupancy remain valid.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: Setting competitor concentration to zero, or taking its affinity to be negligible, recovers the parent Hill law.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Vary L and competitor concentration across samples while holding receptor abundance, background, and rapid-equilibrium conditions fixed: then increasing competitor causes a rightward shift and suppression of the ligand occupancy curve, so samples with the same L but different competitor show different f_bound values.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single parent parameter set can only generate one Hill curve with one shared threshold and slope because it has no competitor input. Although one competitor condition could be mimicked by refitting K_d, one shared refit across multiple competitor levels cannot reproduce the systematic competitor-dependent right shifts and occupancy suppression demanded by the joint mapping.

evolution_plan.promotion_reason: A competitive extracellular condition must vary between samples to generate an observable family of occupancy curves; with only L supplied and all parameters fixed, competition cannot be distinguished from a single refit of K_d on one condition.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model omits environmental competition for the same receptor pool, assuming the measured ligand is the only extracellular species influencing rapid equilibrium occupancy.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Relax the assumption of an otherwise fixed extracellular binding environment by allowing a second independently sampled competitor concentration while keeping receptor abundance fixed and rapid equilibrium valid.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Competitive binding by a second extracellular ligand or antagonist that shares the receptor binding pool and reduces occupancy by the measured ligand under rapid equilibrium.
evolution_plan.rationale: Parent response relationship: with extracellular ligand concentration L varying and receptor abundance/background held fixed, f_bound increases monotonically as a single Hill function and approaches a finite ceiling of 1. Scientific gap: real cell-surface binding assays can be performed in the presence of a competitor or antagonist, which changes the target mapping itself, not merely an unobserved auxiliary trajectory. Changed relationship: when competitor concentration varies across samples, the child model should produce a family of monotone ligand-response curves with competitor-dependent right-shift or suppression, i.e. an interaction between ligand level and extracellular environment. Distinguishing condition: vary L and competitor concentration across samples while keeping receptor abundance, background, and rapid-equilibrium assumption fixed; then compare two nonzero competitor levels. A single parent parameter set cannot reproduce both curves because it has one fixed threshold/slope for all samples and no input through which the environment can alter occupancy. This contrast is observable when competitor is in a regime comparable to its own binding scale; if absent or negligible, the parent law is recovered honestly.
